D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official list contains read and write operations, including payroll updates/submission, employee changes, time entry, onboarding and payment-link creation. No readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint annotations are published. 2. Docs recommend manual client approval for every call; Gusto’s product page says every write returns for confirmation. Enforcement by the server is not demonstrated. create_company specifically documents confirmed:false then confirmed:true. 3. OAuth access is scoped to chosen data categories; primary/global admin required. Gusto may limit approved AI providers and eligibility; access can be revoked by disconnecting, tokens refresh automatically. Token lifetime not published. 4. Docs name production, demo, and Anthropic/OpenAI routes; no read-only mode, toolset filter, or MCP endpoint URL parameters documented. 5. Docs say tool parameters are sanitized in logs, full conversation history is not logged, and sensitive signatures, SSNs, and bank numbers are handled in secure Gusto/Plaid flows instead of chat. Scope boundaries are selected during OAuth. 6. List tools: page default 1, per default 25/max 100; update_payroll supports up to 100 employees. Rate thresholds unpublished; 429 with Retry-After. 7. Docs advise removing unsupported arguments and provide invalid-parameter troubleshooting; no detailed validation/correction or argument-override behavior documented. 8. Docs describe logs of tool name, sanitized parameters, timestamp, request ID; OAuth tokens, refresh tokens, company ID, request counts, errors, and response times are collected. Terms also authorize collection of query content and possible monitoring. 9. submit_feedback sends feedback about the integration to its team. get_company_onboarding_package returns plans, add-ons, benefits, and Gusto’s recommended package; pay_ein_filing creates a Stripe checkout link. No feedback prompt text beyond the tool description is published. 10. Docs advise clients to require manual confirmation, review calls, verify outputs, isolate the server, and opt out of model training. No initialize instructions or server-delivered skill is published. 11. Persistent agent memory behavior is undocumented. 12. The published tool list is flat; tools can open Gusto/Plaid flows, report work is queued and polled, and time tracking routes to native or third-party systems. Other endpoints have different routes/tool counts. 13. No raw API, SQL, script execution, or general-purpose request tool appears in the official 72-tool list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: [DOCS] “Do not connect other MCP servers to the same client session that is connected to Gusto.”
[DOCS] “You should always be prompted to confirm any tool call before it is executed.”
[DOCS] “Always verify critical information directly in Gusto.”
[DOCS] “Use the include parameter to request only needed fields”
[DOCS] `create_company`: “call with `confirmed: false` first to verify the account email, then `confirmed: true` to create.”
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The official production reference presents one flat 72-tool list. Separate demo and client-specific routes, secure external flows, and routing to third-party time tracking are documented, but no dynamic toolset or nested server architecture is described.

Counts seen elsewhere are incomplete or for other listings/routes: EveryMCPServer displays 60 of 72; Claude’s directory lists 62 tools at /anthropic; Agentman reports 41; Manufact reports 43. These counts are not substituted for the official list.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code or verbatim tool schemas/initialize instructions were available. The official reference gives names, descriptions, and only shared pagination parameters; it does not provide full serialized tool definitions.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The MCP tools do not collect signatures or SSNs in chat; users complete those steps in secure Gusto flows. EIN filing payment is provided as a Stripe checkout link. An S-Corp election form still must be mailed by the owner to the IRS. The tool list limits workers’ compensation class lookup to Washington and Wyoming. Gusto’s general product interfaces may support other workflows not represented in the published MCP list; this review does not infer their exact availability.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Docs ask the client to require manual confirmation, isolate Gusto MCP sessions, use trusted clients, review calls, verify outputs, and opt out of model training. These are client/user recommendations; the docs do not demonstrate server enforcement for all calls. Gusto’s product page states that every write returns for confirmation, but the enforcement mechanism is unspecified.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Docs say tool-call parameters are sanitized in logs, full conversation history is not logged, and OAuth tokens are stored securely and revoked on disconnect. They say the user may export tool logs and revoke access. The Gusto MCP Terms authorize collection of query content and possible monitoring, and warn that AI providers may train on or retain transmitted data. The Gusto privacy notice says its third-party AI providers are not permitted to train on personal information.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Gusto describes scoped, least-privilege access, user-selected data categories, and manual confirmation of writes. Its legal terms place responsibility for verifying AI output and human oversight on the employer.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth-selected categories and the documented confirmed:false/true create_company flow are concrete controls. The docs recommend client confirmation generally, while the product page claims all writes return for confirmation; server-side enforcement was not independently evidenced. Logging and token handling are documentation claims. The MCP Terms’ query-content collection language conflicts with the docs’ statement that full conversation history is not logged.

contradictions: The input is https://api.gusto.com/v1/mcp, while Gusto’s official docs identify https://mcp.api.gusto.com. The input returned HTTP 200 with JSON-RPC Invalid request, but its protected-resource metadata paths returned 404 and no input-specific tool list was found. The 72-tool list is therefore best-available evidence from the documented endpoint, not endpoint-specific confirmation.

The pre-fetched OAuth metadata is for api.gusto.com; the documented MCP host is mcp.api.gusto.com. The metadata scopes and OAuth server details are not verified as the scopes used by the documented MCP endpoint.

The official docs list 72 tools, while third-party catalogues report partial counts (EveryMCPServer 60/72, Agentman 41, Manufact 43). Claude’s directory lists 62 tools for the separate /anthropic route. These figures do not match the main official list and may reflect partial listings or route differences.

Gusto MCP docs say full conversation history is not logged, but Gusto MCP Terms authorize collecting the content of queries made through the linked LLM account. The relationship between these statements is not clarified in the available material.

The Gusto product page says every write returns for confirmation; the technical docs recommend client-side manual confirmation. The available material does not specify how the write confirmation is enforced.
observations_for_research: The published tool list spans payroll reads and writes, employee administration, time entry, onboarding, tax-form preparation, estimates, and vendor feedback.
The docs combine OAuth data-category selection with explicit client-side behavioral recommendations and separate secure flows for sensitive information.
Some tool descriptions include operational constraints or behavioral wording, including two-stage company creation, no SSN collection in chat, and a constrained tax qualification verdict.
